clue.text: Thieving birds hide silver and pastry in hollow monuments

indicators.note: to hide something is to tuck it out of sight inside something else, so these two go within
a hollow thing has its inside scooped away, leaving only the shell at either end

blocks.note: only the first and last letters of the word survive
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: Birds stash stolen silver and a bit of pastry inside great empty memorials.
explanation.walkthrough: MAGPIES are notorious for snatching shiny objects, which is why 'Thieving' sits so naturally in front of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Magpies are crows famed in folklore for stealing glittering trinkets, so they are the classic thieving birds.

clue.text: Unmarried lady takes in a model with Eastern artist

indicators.note: taking someone in means admitting them inside, so the lady's title wraps around what follows

blocks.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman
taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: A single woman brings a fashion model and someone from the East along with her.
explanation.walkthrough: MATISSE: A and T go inside MISS, then E follows. 'model' looks like a person posing, but here it is the Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter famous for bold colour and paper cut-outs, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Leaving gift to force student to study those who work on fish

blocks.note: go is drive or energy, stretched here to mean force
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
a den is a private room for study
hands are workers, as in farmhands
hake is a fish of the cod family; on places it last

explanation.surface: A send-off present seems to push a student into studying fishermen.
explanation.walkthrough: GO + L + DEN + HANDS + HAKE gives GOLDEN HANDSHAKE. Reading 'force' as GO (energy, drive) is loose; it is the only way the clue supplies the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden handshake is a generous payment to an employee on retirement or departure, a lavish gift for leaving.

clue.text: Beg a politician to run with energy for a change

indicators.note: doing something for a change means doing it differently, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a means one, which is the Roman numeral I
an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with an MP to stand for office with some vigour, just to shake things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests asking a politician to run for election, but every word after Beg is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to pester someone persistently with requests, which is to beg them repeatedly.

clue.text: Sometimes words conceal a weapon

indicators.note: to conceal is to keep out of sight inside, so the answer is tucked within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: runs from the last letter of the first word through the second word

explanation.surface: A sly remark that what people say can sometimes mask a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: SometimeS WORDs holds SWORD, which also happens to be a rearrangement of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword is a long bladed weapon carried for fighting with an edge and a point.

clue.text: I begin sermon with unusual claim to be of the Muslim faith

indicators.note: to begin the word is to take only its opening letter
unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the word
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A preacher opens a sermon with an odd assertion about religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic is the adjective for Islam, the religion whose followers are Muslims, so it describes the Muslim faith.

clue.text: Northerner chucked out rancid eel

indicators.note: something chucked out is thrown about carelessly, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fisherman from the north throws away an eel that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander lives in Iceland, near the Arctic Circle, so is a person from the far north.

clue.text: Oaf gains aspiration to reach this Lincolnshire town

blocks.note: a lout is a clumsy, ill-mannered person
the letter h stands for the breathy sound called aspiration

explanation.surface: A boorish man arrives in a small English market town with big ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' reads as ambition, but in phonetics it is the breathed sound of the letter h. Lincolnshire is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Louth is a market town in Lincolnshire, in the east of England, so it is an example of such a town.

clue.text: Mafia king relies foolishly on alibi about way of delivering books

indicators.note: acting foolishly means not in a sensible order, so these letters get jumbled
about means turned around and scattered, so these letters join the jumble too

blocks.note: the Mob is a name for the Mafia
R for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangland boss leans stupidly on a flimsy excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: MOB is kept as is; R plus RELIES and ALIBI are mixed up to give ILE LIBRARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile libraries are vans that carry lending stock around towns and villages, a way of bringing books to readers.

clue.text: Grow half a carrot from seed plant

indicators.note: half of the word means only its first three letters of six are kept

blocks.note: the front half of the vegetable's name
taken as written
from suggests away, read loosely as a way off

explanation.surface: A gardener tries to raise half a carrot from seed.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR + A + WAY. The surface is all about growing vegetables, which hides that the answer is a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Caraway is a herb of the parsley family grown for its aromatic seeds, used to flavour bread and cakes.

clue.text: Help ET out with a single figure - he'll need it to call home

definitions.text: he'll need it to call home

indicators.note: out suggests broken out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a single thing is one
a figure is a number

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to help the stranded alien from the film, who famously wanted to phone home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the line 'ET phone home' from Spielberg's film: to call home, ET needs a number to dial.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone number is the sequence of digits you dial to ring a particular line, needed for any call home.

clue.text: 'Tis close, we hear, to ridicule

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the words before are judged by how they are spoken

blocks.note: 'tis is it is; shorten that to 's and close means near

explanation.surface: A poetic voice says something is near, then turns to mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneer is to show scorn with a contemptuous smile or remark, which is a way to ridicule someone.

clue.text: Bat howled dreadfully at the fatal stroke

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is badly mangled, so these letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bat screeched horribly at the moment it was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: A death blow is a strike that kills, or figuratively a setback that finishes something off, so a fatal stroke.

clue.text: Weary old lover takes house in Germany to cut tedium by half

indicators.note: to cut a word is to chop part of it off
by half says exactly how much is lost: three letters of the six go

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
Haus is the German word for house
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A tired former partner moves into a German home to relieve some of the boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: EX + HAUS + TED, keeping the first half of tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted means completely drained of energy, a stronger synonym for weary.

clue.text: To tease bird I'll eat nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters before it go haywire

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone taunts a bird by announcing they will eat nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the food the bird might want, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse someone playfully, which is to tease them.

clue.text: Intimidate Jim Bowen's old quiz partner!

blocks.note: first meaning: to frighten or push someone around
second meaning: the cartoon bull mascot of a British TV darts quiz

explanation.surface: A nod to a long-running game show and its cartoon sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: Jim Bowen hosted Bullseye, a British TV quiz built around darts, whose mascot was a cartoon bull called Bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully is to coerce through threats, and Bully was the bull mascot on Bowen's show Bullseye.

clue.text: However, Mr Lawrence took the royal trophy for his flower

blocks.note: however and but both introduce a contrast
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, by his initials
R for rex or regina, the monarch
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A man named Lawrence wins a regal prize and is rewarded with a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower of meadows, so it is an example of a flower.

clue.text: Hidden gas in geyser may burn

indicators.note: the clue states outright that the answer sits concealed in the words that follow

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word across the middle one into the third

explanation.surface: A warning that unseen gas inside a water heater could scorch you.
explanation.walkthrough: A geyser is the British name for a gas water heater, which makes the burning surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn something lightly on the surface, such as hair or the edge of cloth.

clue.text: Bird hits back, leading to noisy dispute

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word for hits is read from its end

blocks.note: raps are sharp knocks
a row is a loud quarrel

explanation.surface: A bird strikes back in retaliation, sparking a loud squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown and grey songbird common around houses, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Models competent to carry vase onto revolving platform

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so the vessel goes inside

blocks.note: two Model Ts, the Ford car, one T each
able means capable
an urn is a large vase

explanation.surface: Skilled fashion models are asked to carry a vase up onto a rotating stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' sounds like people on a catwalk, but it is the plural of the Ford Model T, so it gives two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A turntable is a rotating disc or stage, such as the one a record player spins or a railway locomotive turns on.

clue.text: Friendly relations with opponents established up to a point under canvas

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
in a down clue, under means placed below the following piece

blocks.note: North and East sit on opposing sides at the bridge table
to be under canvas is to be camping in a tent
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Peace with rivals is reached, but only partly, at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play against East-West, so N and E are opponents. ENTENTE is the word meant; the grid's ENTENDE is a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale between Britain and France.

clue.text: Motorists club travel round rocky American trail to the country

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the following word's letters are jumbled
to travel round something is to go all the way about it, enclosing it

blocks.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
US for United States
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A motoring club tours along a rough American trail on its way to a far-off land.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, the breakdown-recovery club.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a nation occupying a whole continent in the southern hemisphere, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Just straighten up

blocks.note: first meaning: fair and morally correct
second meaning: to set something upright again, as with a capsized boat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb meaning only, but here it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for what is fair and proper, and a verb for restoring something to an upright position.

clue.text: A venomous mathematician?

blocks.note: surface reading: a poisonous creature, a snake
setter's reading: someone who sums numbers together

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both Britain's only venomous snake and, read literally, one who adds up figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the common European viper and, punningly, a person or machine that performs addition.

clue.text: Stick up tax as sanction

indicators.note: in this clue, up means turned the other way, so the word for stick is read backwards

blocks.note: a cane is a walking stick
the opening letter, a loose abbreviation the clue does not signal

explanation.surface: A demand to raise taxes, presented as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick up' looks like a phrase for robbery, but it is a stick turned upside down. Taking T for tax is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a measure is to make it law, giving it official approval, which is to sanction it.

clue.text: About raid can't argue, or there'll be fighting at the back

indicators.note: about means turned around and scattered, so the words that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that if you won't dispute the raid, there will be trouble behind the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard action is a defensive fight by troops covering a retreat, literally combat at the rear.

clue.text: We are taking long breather before fight

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the pronoun wraps the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
a breather is a short rest
L abbreviates long, as in long. for longitude

explanation.surface: We take a long pause for breath before a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long breather' suggests a lengthy pause, but long supplies only a single letter, the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple with an opponent and try to throw them, a form of fighting.

clue.text: Rhode Island poet's outburst provokes witty retort

indicators.note: an outburst blows things apart, so the poet's letters are scattered

blocks.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An American poet's angry outburst draws a clever comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, clever reply; the word comes from fencing, where it is a counter-thrust.
